correctness.rationale: For f(p^j)=-1,-1,+1,0 (j=1,2,3,>=4), the Euler polynomial (1-z)(1-z^2) gives f(n)=sum_{d^2|n}mu(d)mu(n/d^2), and f^2=1_{4th-power-free}=sum_{d^4|n}mu(d). For any reduced b mod fixed q, PNT-AP cancels mu in each fixed inner class, while d>T contributes O(x/T). Every nonreduced progression restricted to f!=0 splits into finitely many factors supported at primes dividing q (exponents <=3), reducing to reduced classes; hence sum f=o_q(x). For support, CRT gives exactly one class modulo qd^4/gcd(q,d^4), if gcd(q,d^4)|a, with O(1) counting error. Summing d<=x^1/4 and estimating the tail using gcd<=q yields O_q(x^1/4). The Euler factors produce the asserted kappa; kappa=0 iff p^4|gcd(q,a), otherwise positive. Addition/subtraction proves the three densities. q=1, arbitrary a, nonunits, and e>=4 all satisfy the conditions. The independent finite test directly recomputed the convolution and 339 exact support progression counts up to 120000, without being used as an infinite proof.
residual_risks: No effective o_q(x) error rate, and no uniformity when q grows.
The exact infinite cancellation requires PNT-AP; finite computational checks certify only their finite inputs.

limitations: q is fixed; no growing-modulus uniformity.
Signed discrepancy is o_q(x) without an effective rate.

value.rationale: The three-way distribution is a natural and complete invariant for the new square-splitting Möbius function, specifically motivated by the identical source paper’s distribution questions. It determines all fixed progressions, including noncoprime classes, proves exact equal positive/negative densities when not arithmetically forbidden, gives the full Euler product and an if-and-only-if fourth-power obstruction, with quantitative support error. It is concise and uses standard inputs, but is not a single textbook identity or an arbitrary parameter slice; the exact local spectrum is mathematically meaningful.
residual_risks: Value is in the complete local classification, not new zero-free region or improved analytic estimate.
Future work may require finer sign errors or uniform-in-q estimates, neither established here.
